title: Minuet in G major, BWV Anh. 114
subtitle: from the Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach (1725)
trains: Two independent lines in 3/4: a right-hand melody of stepwise eighth-note runs and leaps against a left hand that moves in its own line of mostly dotted-half, half and quarter notes; mordents (bars 3, 5, 11, 13), a grace note in bar 8 and a short trill in bar 30, and a second half that turns to D major (C sharp) before coming home. Both halves repeated.

provenance.credit: Typeset by Allen Garvin for the Mutopia Project (Mutopia-2017/01/19-75) from the Bach-Gesellschaft edition, and placed in the public domain by the typesetter.
provenance.note: Converted from Mutopia's LilyPond source to MusicXML by pnpm library:convert-ly (notes, rests, repeats and voltas, grace notes, clefs, slurs, dynamics); beams and accidentals then completed by pnpm library:engrave. Checked mechanically against the LilyPond source and Mutopia's own MIDI file (audit record). Long known as "Bach's Minuet in G"; the Notebook copy is unsigned and it is now attributed to Christian Petzold (1677-1733), as the source itself notes.

limitations: The short trill in bar 30 (printed as a Pralltriller sign, MusicXML inverted-mordent; in Baroque practice started from the upper note, on the beat) is printed but not realised: it is neither played along nor excused in grading, and opening the piece shows an information notice about it.
